question: What is the name of the festival that ends the Holy Ramzan month?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eid- Ul- Fitr.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Eid-ul-Fitr marks the end of the holy month of Ramzan (Ramadan), the Islamic month of fasting (Roza). (ईद-उल-फितर — रमजान के अंत का त्योहार)

 

• It falls on the first day of Shawwal, the tenth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, and is celebrated with special prayers (Namaz), charity (Zakat-ul-Fitr) and festive meals.

 

• The festival celebrates the completion of a month of dawn-to-dusk fasting, self-restraint and increased devotion observed throughout Ramzan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bakrid (Eid-ul-Adha) is celebrated about 70 days after Eid-ul-Fitr and commemorates the willingness of Prophet Ibrahim to sacrifice his son.

 

• Muharram marks the beginning of the Islamic New Year and is especially significant for Shia Muslims as a period of mourning for Imam Hussain.

 

NOTE

 

• Muharram (Option 2): It is the first month of the Islamic calendar, not the festival ending Ramzan.

 

• Eid- Ul- Zuha (Option 3): This is another name for Bakrid, celebrated around two months after Ramzan, not at its end.

 

• Bakrid (Option 4): Also called Eid-ul-Adha, it is the 'Festival of Sacrifice', unrelated to the end of Ramzan fasting.

question: The Palas were:
option_1: a dynasty that appeared in Puri
option_2: a dynasty that first appeared in Cambodia
option_3: a dynasty that united eastern India and Burma
option_4: a dynasty that appeared in eastern India
solution_text:
The correct answer is a dynasty that appeared in eastern India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pala Dynasty was a ruling power that emerged in eastern India, primarily controlling the regions of Bengal and Bihar, from the 8th to the 12th century CE. (पाल वंश — पूर्वी भारत)

 

• It was founded by Gopala around 750 CE, who was elected king to end a period of anarchy (Matsyanyaya) in Bengal.

 

• The Palas were staunch patrons of Buddhism and established renowned centres of learning such as Vikramashila and Odantapuri, and also revived Nalanda.

 

• Notable rulers included Dharmapala and Devapala, under whom the empire reached its zenith, extending influence over large parts of northern India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Palas are credited with developing a distinctive school of art and sculpture known as the Pala school of art, which influenced Buddhist art in Nepal and Tibet.

 

• The Palas were eventually succeeded in Bengal by the Sena dynasty.

 

NOTE

 

• A dynasty that appeared in Puri (Option 1): Puri in Odisha is associated with the Gajapati dynasty and the Jagannath Temple, not the Palas.

 

• A dynasty that first appeared in Cambodia (Option 2): The Palas did not originate in Cambodia; Cambodia's ancient kingdoms (like the Khmer Empire) were a separate Southeast Asian civilisation.

 

• A dynasty that united eastern India and Burma (Option 3): The Palas did not politically unite eastern India with Burma (Myanmar); their influence was largely confined to the Indian subcontinent.

question: The largest inland salt lake ‘Sambhar’ is located in the_________of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is north-west.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sambhar Salt Lake, India's largest inland saltwater lake, is located in the state of Rajasthan, which lies in the north-west of India. (साम्भर झील — राजस्थान, उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत)

 

• It is situated between the districts of Jaipur, Nagaur and Ajmer, roughly 80 km from Jaipur.

 

• The lake is a saline wetland fed by rivers such as Mendha, Rupangarh and Khari, and produces a significant share of India's salt.

 

• It is designated as a Ramsar site (wetland of international importance) and serves as an important habitat for migratory birds, especially flamingos.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rajasthan also hosts the Thar Desert, the largest hot desert in India, located in the north-west of the state.

 

• Other notable salt lakes in India include Didwana and Pachpadra, also in Rajasthan.

 

NOTE

 

• north-east (Option 1): The north-eastern states (Assam, Meghalaya, etc.) do not host Sambhar Lake.

 

• south-east (Option 2): The south-eastern part of India includes states like Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, not Rajasthan.

 

• south-west (Option 3): The south-western coast includes Kerala and Karnataka, unrelated to Sambhar Lake's location.

question: In India, the musical instrument “Flute” is also known as _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bansuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The flute, made traditionally of bamboo, is known in India as the Bansuri. (बांसुरी — वायु वाद्य यंत्र/बांस की बनी बांसुरी)

 

• It is a side-blown (transverse) wind instrument closely associated with Lord Krishna in Indian mythology and iconography.

 

• The Bansuri is a key melodic instrument in Hindustani classical music, with Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia being one of its most celebrated exponents.

 

• It typically has six or seven finger holes and produces sound through the resonance of air blown across an embouchure hole.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The South Indian (Carnatic) equivalent flute is called the Venu or Pullanguzhal.

 

• Other classical wind instruments of India include the Shehnai and Nadaswaram.

 

NOTE

 

• Tabla (Option 1): A pair of hand drums used as a percussion instrument, not a wind instrument.

 

• Manjira (Option 2): Small hand cymbals, a percussion instrument used to keep rhythm, especially in devotional music.

 

• Veena (Option 4): A plucked string instrument, one of the oldest instruments of India, not a wind instrument.

question: According to Global Multidimensional poverty index (2022), On the basis of four indicators- nutrition, cooking fuel, sanitation and housing, how much poor people live in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 34.4 million.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2022, released by UNDP and OPHI (Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative), reported that of the over 45.5 million people worldwide who are poor solely on the basis of the four indicators - nutrition, cooking fuel, sanitation and housing - about 34.4 million live in India. (वैश्विक बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2022 — भारत में 34.4 मिलियन गरीब)

 

• This 'deprivation bundle' profile was found to be predominantly South Asian, with the remaining such poor concentrated in Bangladesh (about 2.1 million) and Pakistan (about 1.9 million).

 

• The Global MPI 2022 report was titled 'Unpacking deprivation bundles to reduce multidimensional poverty'.

 

• Separately, the report also highlighted that 415 million people moved out of multidimensional poverty in India between 2005-06 and 2019-21, a historic reduction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Global MPI is jointly published by the UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI), University of Oxford.

 

• India also releases its own National Multidimensional Poverty Index, prepared by NITI Aayog.

 

NOTE

 

• 24.4 million (Option 1): Not the figure cited in the 2022 Global MPI report for this specific deprivation bundle.

 

• 54.4 million (Option 2): Incorrect figure; overstates the reported number for India.

 

• 44.4 million (Option 3): Incorrect figure; close to but not the actual reported value of 34.4 million.

question: In Microsoft Excel, which chart type is best suited for comparing proportions or percentages of a whole?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pie Chart.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Pie Chart in Microsoft Excel displays data as slices of a circle, where each slice represents a category's proportion or percentage of the whole. (पाई चार्ट — संपूर्ण के अनुपात/प्रतिशत की तुलना)

 

• It is specifically designed to show part-to-whole relationships, making it ideal when there is a single data series and the values sum to a meaningful total (100%).

 

• Each slice's angular size and area are proportional to its percentage contribution, allowing quick visual comparison of relative shares.

 

• Pie charts work best with a small number of categories; too many slices make the chart cluttered and hard to interpret.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Excel also offers a Doughnut Chart, which is similar to a pie chart but can display multiple data series as concentric rings.

 

• A 100% Stacked Bar/Column Chart can also show proportions of a whole across multiple categories or time periods.

 

NOTE

 

• Bar Chart (Option 2): Best suited for comparing quantities across different categories, not proportions of a single whole.

 

• Scatter Chart (Option 3): Used to show the relationship or correlation between two numeric variables, not part-to-whole comparisons.

 

• Line Chart (Option 4): Best suited for showing trends in data over a continuous period, not proportions.

question: Who wrote the book ‘Gulamgiri’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jyotiba Phule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Gulamgiri' (Slavery) was written by Mahatma Jyotiba Phule and published in 1873. (गुलामगिरी — ज्योतिबा फुले)

 

• The book is a powerful critique of the caste system and Brahminical social order, drawing a parallel between the condition of the 'lower castes' in India and slavery in the United States.

 

• Phule dedicated the book to the American abolitionists who fought to end the slavery of Black people.

 

• He also founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873, an organisation aimed at securing rights for the oppressed classes, including women and the so-called lower castes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jyotiba Phule is also known for his other works like 'Sarvajanik Satyadharma' and for pioneering girls' education in India, along with his wife Savitribai Phule.

 

• He is popularly referred to as 'Mahatma', a title conferred on him for his social reform work.

 

NOTE

 

• Dwarkanath Tagore (Option 2): An entrepreneur and reformer associated with the Brahmo Samaj, grandfather of Rabindranath Tagore; did not write Gulamgiri.

 

• Swami Shraddhanand (Option 3): A social reformer associated with the Arya Samaj and the Shuddhi movement; did not write Gulamgiri.

 

• BR Ambedkar (Option 4): A key social reformer and architect of the Indian Constitution; his notable works include 'Annihilation of Caste', not Gulamgiri, though he was influenced by Phule.

question: In cost theory, the usual shape of the ________ curve is a rectangular hyperbola.
solution_text:
The correct answer is average fixed cost.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Average Fixed Cost (AFC) curve is typically shaped like a rectangular hyperbola. (औसत स्थिर लागत वक्र — आयताकार अतिपरवलय)

 

• This is because AFC = Total Fixed Cost (TFC) / Output (Q), and since TFC remains constant regardless of output, AFC keeps falling continuously as output rises, but never touches either axis.

 

• As output increases, the fixed cost gets spread over more units, so AFC declines sharply at first and then more gradually, approaching (but never reaching) zero — the classic property of a rectangular hyperbola where the product of the two axes' values (here, AFC x Q = TFC, a constant) remains fixed.

 

• This continuously downward-sloping curve is also called the 'spreading effect' of fixed costs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Average Variable Cost (AVC) and Average Total Cost (ATC) curves are typically U-shaped, reflecting the law of variable proportions.

 

• The Marginal Cost (MC) curve is also U-shaped and intersects the AVC and ATC curves at their minimum points.

 

NOTE

 

• total cost (Option 1): The Total Cost (TC) curve rises continuously with output and is generally S-shaped (or inverse S-shaped), not a rectangular hyperbola.

 

• fixed cost (Option 2): The Total Fixed Cost (TFC) curve is a horizontal straight line, since it does not change with output.

 

• variable cost (Option 4): The Total Variable Cost (TVC) curve is typically an inverse S-shaped curve that rises with output.

question: Which of the following sequences is correct, according to taxonomy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Phylum-Class-Order-Family-Genus-Species.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The standard hierarchy of biological taxonomy, from broadest to most specific (below Kingdom), is: Phylum - Class - Order - Family - Genus - Species. (जैविक वर्गीकरण क्रम — संघ-वर्ग-गण-कुल-वंश-जाति)

 

• This classification system was pioneered by Carl Linnaeus, the 'Father of Taxonomy', who introduced the system of binomial nomenclature.

 

• The full hierarchy, including the topmost rank, is: Kingdom - Phylum - Class - Order - Family - Genus - Species, often remembered by the mnemonic 'King Phillip Came Over For Good Soup'.

 

• Each successive rank groups organisms with progressively finer shared characteristics, with Species being the most specific and basic unit of classification.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In botany, the term 'Division' is often used in place of 'Phylum'.

 

• Modern taxonomy also recognises Domain as a rank above Kingdom, dividing life into Archaea, Bacteria and Eukarya.

 

NOTE

 

• Class-Phylum-Family-Order Genus-Species (Option 1): Incorrectly places Class before Phylum and Family before Order, disrupting the correct hierarchy.

 

• Family-Phylum-Class-Order-Genus-Species (Option 2): Incorrectly starts with Family, which should appear much later in the sequence.

 

• Class-Phylum-Order-Family-Genus-Species (Option 4): Incorrectly places Class before Phylum, though the rest of the sequence is in order.

question: Which of the following teams won the IPL 2023 championship?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chennai Super Kings.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chennai Super Kings (CSK) won the IPL 2023 title, defeating Gujarat Titans (GT) in a rain-affected final. (आईपीएल 2023 — चेन्नई सुपर किंग्स विजेता)

 

• The final was played on 29 May 2023 at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, and was reduced to a 15-over-a-side match due to rain.

 

• This was CSK's 5th IPL title, equalling Mumbai Indians' record of most IPL championships at the time.

 

• Ravindra Jadeja hit the winning runs off the last ball, and CSK captain MS Dhoni lifted the trophy in what was seen as a landmark moment of his career.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gujarat Titans, the finalists in IPL 2023, had won the IPL 2022 title in their debut season under captain Hardik Pandya.

 

• The Orange Cap (highest run-scorer) in IPL 2023 went to Shubman Gill, and the Purple Cap (highest wicket-taker) went to Mohammed Shami.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat Titans (Option 1): They were the runners-up in IPL 2023, having won the title the previous year (2022).

 

• Mumbai Indians (Option 2): A five-time IPL champion (2013, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2020), but did not win the 2023 title.

 

• Lucknow SuperGiants (Option 3): They did not reach the IPL 2023 final; the finalists were CSK and GT.

question: Norman Ernest Borlaug was awarded the _____ in 1970 for his contributions to the green revolution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nobel Peace Prize.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Norman Ernest Borlaug, an American agronomist, was awarded the 1970 Nobel Peace Prize for his contributions to the Green Revolution, which greatly increased global food production and is credited with saving millions of people from starvation. (नॉर्मन बोरलॉग — 1970 नोबेल शांति पुरस्कार)

 

• He is often called the 'Father of the Green Revolution', having developed high-yielding, disease-resistant varieties of wheat, particularly through his work in Mexico.

 

• His work was extended to India and Pakistan in the 1960s, contributing significantly to India's own Green Revolution alongside scientists such as M. S. Swaminathan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Borlaug is one of only a handful of people to have received the Nobel Peace Prize, the Presidential Medal of Freedom, and the Congressional Gold Medal — the three highest civilian honours in the United States.

 

• M. S. Swaminathan, regarded as the father of India's Green Revolution, worked closely with Borlaug in introducing high-yield wheat varieties to India.

 

NOTE

 

• Nobel Prize in Physiology (Option 2): Awarded annually for discoveries in medicine/physiology (e.g., to scientists for work on genetics, immunology, etc.) — Borlaug's award was in a different category, Peace, not Physiology.

 

• Nobel Prize in Chemistry (Option 3): Awarded for outstanding contributions in chemistry; not the prize Borlaug received.

 

• Nobel Prize in Physics (Option 4): Awarded for outstanding contributions in physics; not the prize Borlaug received.

question: Who among the following discovered that a wire carrying electric current can attract or repel another wire next to it that's also carrying electric current?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andre-Marie Ampere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Andre-Marie Ampere, a French physicist, discovered that two parallel current-carrying wires exert a force on each other - attracting if the currents flow in the same direction, and repelling if they flow in opposite directions. (आंद्रे-मैरी एम्पीयर — विद्युत धारावाही तारों के बीच आकर्षण/प्रतिकर्षण)

 

• This discovery, made in 1820, laid the foundation of the field of electrodynamics, and Ampere is often called the 'Father of Electrodynamics'.

 

• The SI unit of electric current, the Ampere (A), is named in his honour.

 

• His work built upon Hans Christian Oersted's discovery that an electric current produces a magnetic field, extending it to explain the mutual forces between current-carrying conductors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ampere's Circuital Law, a fundamental law in electromagnetism, relates the integrated magnetic field around a closed loop to the electric current passing through it.

 

• This principle underlies the working of devices like electromagnets and electric motors.

 

NOTE

 

• Michael Faraday (Option 1): Known for discovering electromagnetic induction, not the force between current-carrying wires.

 

• Guglielmo Marconi (Option 3): Known as a pioneer of long-distance radio transmission (wireless telegraphy).

 

• James Maxwell (Option 4): Known for formulating the Maxwell's equations, which unify electricity, magnetism and light, but not for this specific discovery.

question: Which Articles of the Constitution deal with citizenship?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Articles 5 to 11.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Citizenship is dealt with under Part II of the Indian Constitution, comprising Articles 5 to 11. (नागरिकता — संविधान का भाग II, अनुच्छेद 5 से 11)

 

• Article 5 deals with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution; Article 6 covers rights of citizenship for persons who migrated from Pakistan; Article 7 covers rights of citizenship for migrants to Pakistan.

 

• Article 8 deals with rights of citizenship of persons of Indian origin residing outside India; Article 9 deals with persons voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign state.

 

• Article 10 provides for continuance of the rights of citizenship; Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law - which it did through the Citizenship Act, 1955.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Citizenship Act, 1955 provides for acquisition of citizenship by birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, and incorporation of territory.

 

• The Constitution provides for a single citizenship for the whole of India, unlike some federal countries that have dual citizenship (national and state).

 

NOTE

 

• Articles 5 to 10 (Option 2): Incomplete, as it omits Article 11, which is a crucial provision empowering Parliament to legislate on citizenship.

 

• Articles 5 to 8 (Option 3): Incomplete, omitting Articles 9, 10 and 11.

 

• Articles 5 to 9 (Option 4): Incomplete, omitting Articles 10 and 11.

question: The establishment of Union Public Service Commission, State Public Service Commissions and Joint Public Service Commission falls under which of the following features of the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Federalism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Constitution provides for a Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) for the Centre and State Public Service Commissions (SPSCs) for the states, reflecting the federal structure of governance where powers and institutions are distributed between the Union and the States. (संघवाद — संघ लोक सेवा आयोग और राज्य लोक सेवा आयोग)

 

• Article 315 provides for these Public Service Commissions, while Article 315(2) allows two or more states to agree to have a Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC), upon a resolution passed by their respective legislatures and a law made by Parliament.

 

• This arrangement, allowing for both central and state-level institutions to recruit civil servants independently, is a manifestation of the division of powers central to a federal polity.

 

• The chairman and members of the UPSC are appointed by the President, while those of a SPSC are appointed by the Governor of the respective state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 320 deals with the functions of the Public Service Commissions, primarily relating to recruitment and disciplinary matters for civil services.

 

• Public Service Commissions are constitutional bodies mentioned in Part XIV of the Constitution, which deals with 'Services under the Union and the States'.

 

NOTE

 

• Parliamentary Government (Option 2): Refers to the executive being responsible to the legislature (Council of Ministers responsible to Parliament/State Legislature), not to the structure of Public Service Commissions.

 

• Directive Principles of State Policy (Option 3): These are non-justiciable guidelines in Part IV of the Constitution aimed at establishing social and economic democracy, unrelated to Public Service Commissions.

 

• Fundamental Rights (Option 4): These are justiciable rights guaranteed to citizens under Part III of the Constitution, unrelated to the establishment of Public Service Commissions.

question: Chhannulal Mishra is related to which Musical Lineage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kirana Musical Family.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Chhannulal Mishra is a renowned Hindustani classical vocalist, particularly known for Khayal, Thumri, Kajri and Chaiti, and is associated with the Kirana Gharana, having trained under Ustad Abdul Ghani Khan of this gharana. (छन्नूलाल मिश्र — किराना घराना)

 

• He is closely identified with the musical culture of Banaras (Varanasi), and is also referred to as an exponent of the Banaras style of singing devotional and light-classical forms.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (2010) and later the Padma Vibhushan (2022), India's second-highest civilian award, in recognition of his contribution to Hindustani classical music.

 

• He also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his mastery over Thumri and Kajri singing styles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kirana Gharana was founded by Ustad Abdul Karim Khan and Ustad Abdul Wahid Khan, and is known for its emphasis on slow, meditative melodic development (raga elaboration).

 

• Other prominent Kirana Gharana artists include Pandit Bhimsen Joshi and Gangubai Hangal.

 

NOTE

 

• Agara Musical Family (Option 1): The Agra Gharana is a different Hindustani classical tradition, known for its 'Nom-Tom' style of Khayal singing, not associated with Chhannulal Mishra.

 

• Delhi Musical Family (Option 2): The Delhi Gharana is a distinct gharana known for a balanced style incorporating both Dhrupad and Khayal elements.

 

• Jaipur Musical Family (Option 4): The Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana, founded by Ustad Alladiya Khan, is a separate tradition known for complex, less-common ragas.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, which of the following states is the most urbanised?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Census of India 2011, Goa is the most urbanised state in India, with an urban population of about 62.17%. (जनगणना 2011 — सर्वाधिक शहरीकृत राज्य: गोवा)

 

• Among Union Territories, Delhi recorded the highest level of urbanisation (nearly 97.5%), but since Delhi is a UT, it is excluded when ranking 'states'.

 

• Goa's small geographical size, along with concentrated industrial, tourism-related and mining activity, has contributed to its exceptionally high level of urbanisation compared to other Indian states.

 

• As per Census 2011, India's overall urban population stood at about 31.16% of the total population.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Himachal Pradesh recorded one of the lowest levels of urbanisation among Indian states as per Census 2011 (around 10%).

 

• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of India and the 7th after Independence, with the theme 'Our Census, Our Future'.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 2): Though highly developed with a near-continuous urban-rural landscape, its official urbanisation rate (around 47.7%) as per Census 2011 was lower than Goa's.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): One of the least urbanised states in India, predominantly rural in character.

 

• Punjab (Option 4): Its urbanisation rate (around 37.5%) as per Census 2011 was also lower than Goa's.

question: On 7 November 2022, the Supreme Court of India upheld the reservations for the weaker sections (EWS). Which of the following amendments brought this reservation in the first place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 103rd Amendment of the Constitution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 introduced 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in government jobs and educational institutions, by inserting Article 15(6) and Article 16(6) into the Constitution. (103वां संविधान संशोधन — आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्ग आरक्षण)

 

• On 7 November 2022, a 5-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court, in the case of Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India, upheld the validity of this amendment by a 3:2 majority.

 

• The EWS quota applies to those from the 'general' (unreserved) category who are not already covered by existing SC/ST/OBC reservation schemes, based on defined income and asset criteria.

 

• The majority held that reservation solely on the basis of economic criteria does not violate the basic structure of the Constitution, and that excluding SC/ST/OBC candidates from the EWS quota (since they already have separate reservation) is not discriminatory.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 50% ceiling on total reservations, laid down in the Indra Sawhney case (1992), was held by the majority to not apply as an absolute, inflexible rule for this specific EWS provision.

 

• The 101st Amendment (2016) introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST), unrelated to reservations.

 

NOTE

 

• 102nd Amendment (Option 2): Granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC).

 

• 104th Amendment (Option 3): Extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies but discontinued the reservation for the Anglo-Indian community.

 

• 101st Amendment (Option 4): Introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India, unrelated to EWS reservation.

question: The moderate margin of a page in MS Word can be applied to the page from which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Page Layout Tab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Microsoft Word, page Margins (including preset options like Normal, Moderate, Narrow and Wide) are applied via the Page Layout Tab (called 'Layout' in newer versions), under the 'Margins' option in the Page Setup group. (पृष्ठ लेआउट टैब — मार्जिन सेटिंग)

 

• The 'Moderate' margin preset typically sets 1 inch top/bottom and 0.75 inch left/right margins, offering slightly more usable page width than the 'Normal' preset.

 

• The Page Layout/Layout tab also houses other page-formatting tools such as Orientation, Size, Columns, Breaks, and Paragraph spacing.

 

• Custom margins can also be set from this tab by selecting 'Custom Margins' and entering specific measurements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Design Tab in MS Word is used for applying document themes, colors, fonts, and page borders/watermarks.

 

• The View Tab is used to switch between different document views like Print Layout, Web Layout, Read Mode, and to toggle rulers and gridlines.

 

NOTE

 

• Design Tab (Option 2): Used for overall document styling (themes, colors, watermarks), not for setting page margins.

 

• Review tab (Option 3): Used for proofing tools like Spelling & Grammar check, Track Changes, and Comments.

 

• View Tab (Option 4): Used to change how the document is displayed on screen, not to set margins.

question: Who was the first Indian woman wrestler to win a medal at the Olympics?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sakshi Malik.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sakshi Malik became the first Indian woman wrestler to win an Olympic medal, claiming the bronze medal in the 58 kg freestyle category at the 2016 Rio Olympics. (साक्षी मलिक — पहली भारतीय महिला पहलवान ओलंपिक पदक विजेता)

 

• She defeated Aisuluu Tynybekova of Kyrgyzstan in the bronze-medal bout after trailing initially in the match.

 

• Following this historic achievement, she was honoured with the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (India's highest sporting honour) and the Padma Shri.

 

• Her achievement was particularly significant as it broke new ground for Indian women in wrestling at the Olympic level, encouraging greater participation and investment in women's wrestling in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Geeta Phogat was the first Indian woman wrestler to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal (2010 Delhi CWG), but did not win an Olympic medal.

 

• Since Sakshi Malik's feat, other Indian women wrestlers have also gone on to make history at the international level, keeping wrestling a prominent Olympic discipline for India.

 

NOTE

 

• Alka Tomar (Option 1): A veteran Indian wrestler and Arjuna Award winner, but did not win an Olympic medal.

 

• Babita Phogat (Option 2): A Commonwealth Games gold medallist wrestler from the famous Phogat wrestling family, but did not win an Olympic medal.

 

• Geeta Phogat (Option 3): The first Indian woman wrestler to qualify for the Olympics (2012 London) and a Commonwealth Games gold medallist, but she did not win an Olympic medal.

question: ‘Chang dance’ is popular in the state of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Chang Dance' is a traditional folk dance popular in Rajasthan, particularly performed by men during the festival of Holi. (चंग नृत्य — राजस्थान)

 

• It gets its name from the 'Chang', a large, round percussion instrument resembling a tambourine/frame drum, which is played while performing the dance.

 

• The dance is especially prominent in the Shekhawati region of Rajasthan and involves energetic movements, singing of folk songs (often 'Dhamal'), and rhythmic beating of the Chang instrument in a circular formation.

 

• It reflects the vibrant, community-celebratory culture of Rajasthan's folk traditions associated with seasonal festivals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Rajasthan include Ghoomar, Kalbelia, and Kachhi Ghodi.

 

• Kalbelia dance, performed by the Kalbelia tribe of Rajasthan, has been inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

 

NOTE

 

• Goa (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Dekhni and Fugdi, not Chang dance.

 

• Tripura (Option 2): Known for folk dances like Hojagiri, not Chang dance.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Known for folk dances like Jat-Jatin and Jhijhiya, not Chang dance.

question: Who among the following cabinet ministers was appointed as the Governor of Karnataka in July 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thawarchand Gehlot.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thawarchand Gehlot, who was serving as the Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, was appointed as the Governor of Karnataka in July 2021. (थावरचंद गहलोत — कर्नाटक के राज्यपाल, जुलाई 2021)

 

• He assumed office as Governor on 11 July 2021, succeeding Vajubhai Vala.

 

• Before his gubernatorial appointment, Gehlot had a long political career, including as a Rajya Sabha MP from Madhya Pradesh and as a senior BJP leader.

 

• This appointment was part of a broader reshuffle of governors and cabinet ministers around that period in mid-2021.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Governors are appointed by the President of India under Article 155 of the Constitution, and hold office during the pleasure of the President as per Article 156.

 

• Vajubhai Vala, whom Gehlot succeeded, had earlier also served as the Governor of Karnataka and previously held the Kerala governorship.

 

NOTE

 

• Arjun Munda (Option 1): A Union Cabinet Minister (Tribal Affairs) and former Chief Minister of Jharkhand; not appointed as Governor of Karnataka.

 

• Rajendra Vishwanath (Option 2): Not associated with the Karnataka governorship appointment in July 2021.

 

• Hari Babu Kambhampati (Option 4): He served as Governor of Mizoram, not Karnataka.

question: Which dwarf planet orbits the sun in 310 years at a distance between 38.5 to 53 AU?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Makemake.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Makemake, a dwarf planet located in the Kuiper Belt, takes about 305 to 310 years to complete one orbit around the Sun, at a distance ranging from roughly 38.5 AU (perihelion) to 53 AU (aphelion). (मेकमेक — बौना ग्रह, कुइपर बेल्ट)

 

• It was discovered in 2005 by a team led by Mike Brown, and is named after the creator deity of the Rapa Nui people of Easter Island.

 

• Makemake is the second-brightest object in the Kuiper Belt after Pluto, and is classified as a plutoid (a dwarf planet beyond Neptune's orbit).

 

• It has one known small moon, informally nicknamed 'MK2'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The International Astronomical Union (IAU) currently recognises five dwarf planets: Ceres, Pluto, Eris, Haumea, and Makemake.

 

• Ceres is the only dwarf planet located in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter; all the others lie in the outer solar system (Kuiper Belt/scattered disc).

 

NOTE

 

• Ceres (Option 1): Located in the asteroid belt, it has a much shorter orbital period of about 4.6 years, not 310 years.

 

• Eris (Option 2): One of the most distant known dwarf planets, with an orbital period of about 557 years, much longer than 310 years.

 

• Pluto (Option 4): Has an orbital period of about 248 years at a distance of roughly 30 to 49 AU, not matching the figures given.

question: Which country hosted the first FIFA World Cup?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uruguay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first FIFA World Cup was hosted by Uruguay in 1930. (पहला फीफा विश्व कप — उरुग्वे, 1930)

 

• The tournament was held in the capital city Montevideo, and the final was played at the newly built Estadio Centenario.

 

• Uruguay won the inaugural tournament, defeating Argentina 4-2 in the final, and thus became the first-ever FIFA World Cup champions.

 

• Uruguay was chosen as host partly because it was the reigning Olympic football champion (1924 and 1928) and to mark the centenary of its independence in 1930.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The FIFA World Cup is organized by FIFA (Federation Internationale de Football Association) and is held every four years.

 

• Brazil holds the record for winning the most World Cup titles, with 5 titles (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002).

 

NOTE

 

• Brazil (Option 1): Hosted the World Cup in 1950 and 2014, not the first edition.

 

• Italy (Option 2): Hosted the 1934 (second edition) and 1990 World Cups, not the first.

 

• France (Option 4): Hosted the 1938 and 1998 World Cups, not the first.

question: Dinesh K Tripathi was appointed as ______ in January, 2024
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vice Chief of Naval Staff.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vice Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi was appointed as the Vice Chief of the Naval Staff (VCNS) in January 2024. (दिनेश के त्रिपाठी — नौसेना उप-प्रमुख, जनवरी 2024)

 

• He subsequently went on to become the 26th Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) of the Indian Navy, taking over from Admiral R Hari Kumar on 30 April 2024.

 

• Vice Admiral Tripathi is a specialist in Navigation and Direction, and has held several key operational and staff appointments during his career in the Indian Navy.

 

• As VCNS, he served as the second-in-command of the Indian Navy, before his elevation to the top post.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi's predecessor as CNS, Admiral R Hari Kumar, retired on 30 April 2024.

 

• Vice Admiral Krishna Swaminathan took over as the Vice Chief of Naval Staff on 1 May 2024, after Tripathi's elevation to CNS.

 

NOTE

 

• Chief of Naval Staff (Option 2): Tripathi took over as CNS only in April 2024, not January 2024; in January 2024 he was appointed VCNS.

 

• Rear Admiral (Option 3): This is a lower naval rank; by January 2024 Tripathi already held the higher rank of Vice Admiral.

 

• Chief of Personnel (Option 4): Not the position he was appointed to in January 2024; he was appointed Vice Chief of Naval Staff.

question: According to Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, what was the total food grain production of India in the year 2022-23?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3296.87 lakh tonnes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Third Advance Estimates released by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, India's total food grain production for the year 2022-23 was estimated at a record 3296.87 lakh tonnes (about 329.7 million tonnes). (खाद्यान्न उत्पादन 2022-23 — 3296.87 लाख टन)

 

• This marked an increase over the previous year's production, reflecting a new record in India's foodgrain output.

 

• The rise was driven by higher output of rice, wheat, maize, and pulses, supported by favourable monsoon conditions and government initiatives to boost productivity.

 

• India remained among the largest producers of foodgrains globally, contributing significantly to both domestic food security and exports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare releases estimates in stages - First, Second, Third and Fourth Advance Estimates - before the Final Estimates for a crop year are published.

 

• Rice and wheat together account for the largest share of India's total foodgrain production.

 

NOTE

 

• 2266.23 lakh tonnes (Option 1): Does not match the official 2022-23 estimate for total foodgrain production.

 

• 2876.17 lakh tonnes (Option 2): Does not match the official 2022-23 estimate for total foodgrain production.

 

• 2491.58 lakh tonnes (Option 3): Does not match the official 2022-23 estimate for total foodgrain production.
